THINGS I SUSPECT BUT COULD NOT CONFIRM. The tominersen ventricular-volume increase may reflect increased CSF volume rather than parenchymal atrophy - CHDI 2021 slide 34 reports no drug-related difference in whole-brain or caudate boundary shift integral, which is consistent with that reading, and one review I fetched raises inflammation as an explanation, but no source I read states it as a conclusion. The tofersen authors raise a possible non-inflammatory CSF-outflow-obstruction mechanism for raised intracranial pressure while explicitly reporting no hydrocephalus on imaging in any participant, which is the sharpest available contrast with the valeriasen cases, where hydrocephalus occurred with negative CSF inflammatory markers and was hypothesised to be dose-related. Taken together with the N=1 Collaborative's observation that the valeriasen hydrocephalus was not predicted by healthy-rat safety studies, this is the most valuable translational thread in the lane. The zorevunersen finding of elevated CSF protein in 45% of chronically dosed children in the open-label extensions is the most under-characterised chronic CNS signal here and needs the full text.
